info.title: SmartDok API
info.description:
# How to use API

Make sure that your SmartDok account includes API access. If not, please contact the sales department to get access.

As an administrator, log in to SmartDok, navigate to "Company settings"
and "API administration". On that page, you can generate what we call an API access token.
This gives you a secret token, which is used to get access to the API. This token is valid
for one year at a time.

This token is used to create a session token with [POST /Authorize/ApiToken](/api-docs/#tag/authorize/POST/Authorize/ApiToken).
The session token returned, must be passed in the "Authorization" HTTP header
on all subsequent API calls, after the word "Bearer", by standard convention.

```
Authorization: Bearer SESSION-TOKEN
```

# General

Every resource has a unique URI that consists of the type of resource, and a
unique identifier (e.g. [/Projects/{id}](/api-docs/#tag/projects/GET/Projects/{id})).
Use a GET request to this URI, to retrieve the resource as a JSON object.
Use a GET request to the resource type URI (e.g. [/Projects](/api-docs/#tag/projects/GET/Projects)), to retrieve a list of resources
(various filters are available).

Use POST to the resource type URI, to create new resources, and PUT to update
existing resources. It is an error to try to PUT to a location that doesn't
already contain a resource, because resource identifiers are generated by the
server.

When successful, POST and PUT requests generally return the resulting resource,
as a JSON object. A successful POST request is indicated with the status code
**201 Created**, and the URL for the created resource is contained in the
Location header. A successful PUT request is indicated by the status code **200 OK**.

When a POST or PUT request fails, this is generally indicated by one of the
status codes **404 Not Found** or **400 Bad Request**. Not found simply means
that the URL does not point to a valid resource, and no additional information is provided.
Bad request errors include a JSON object with the following attributes:

- **Code** The error code as a numeric value.
- **Error** The error code as a string (e.g. "NameIsRequired").
- **Message** Textual error message. This is mainly for logging/debugging purposes.

# Updating fields

Generally speaking, all PUT methods in this API will completely _replace_ the
content of the given resource. It works very similar to files in a normal file
system. If you want to change some part of a file, you need to first _load_ the
file, change the content as required, and then _save_ the file back including
all content that you didn't change.

This is done by first using the GET method to fetch the resource, then make
changes to the data that was received, and finally using a PUT request to save
the changes, making sure to include all fields that wasn't changed. To make sure
an integration will work as expected, we recommend that all unknown fields are
passed back with PUT as-is, including fields that might be added in the future.

Code examples of how this can be done are shown below.

### Example: Javascript

```javascript
function updateName(url, name) {
  var getResult = await fetch(url);
  var resource = await getResult.json();
  resource.Name = name;
  var putResult = await fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', data: JSON.stringify(resource) });
  return putResult.ok;
}
```

### Example: .NET

It's a little bit more unconventional in C#, because C# generally deal with known data
structures (classes), and dealing with "unknown" JSON data is less common.

The following examples use [Json.NET](https://www.newtonsoft.com/json).

```csharp
public async Task UpdateName(string url, string name)
{
    var getResult = await _client.GetAsync(url);

    var obj = JObject.Parse(await getResult.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
    obj["Name"] = name;

    var putResult = await _client.PutAsync(url, new StringContent(obj.ToString()));
}
```

Another example, if we have a C# class that contains all the attributes we want
to _update_, say `Project`:

```csharp
public async Task UpdateSmartDokProject(string url, Project data)
{
    var getResult = await _client.GetAsync(url);

    var obj = JObject.Parse(await getResult.Content.ReadAsStringAsync());
    obj.Merge(JObject.FromObject(project));

    var putResult = await _client.PutAsync(url, new StringContent(obj.ToString()));
}
```

# Webhooks

The SmartDok API supports webhooks. To create a webhook, send a POST request to /webhooks with the topic you
want to subscribe to along with a callback URL as a string.

### Supported webhook topics

**- SupplierInvoiceUpdated**

The _SupplierInvoiceUpdated_ topic is currently only triggered when a supplier invoice is approved. The
payload will only return the id of the changed invoice.
You have to query [GET /SupplierInvoices/{id}](/api-docs/#tag/supplierinvoices/GET/SupplierInvoices/{id}) to get the
updated resource.

### Validating request payload

In every webhook request we send a `X-PAYLOAD-SIGNATURE-ALG` and `X-PAYLOAD-SIGNATURE` header value. The signature
is a base64-encoded `RSAPKCS1` signed hash of the payload data itself. The used hash algorithm is specified in the
`X-PAYLOAD-SIGNATURE-ALG` header.

The payload is signed using SmartDok's private keys. To verify the signature, first obtain SmartDok's public keys.
Due to key rotation, we provide a list of public keys, with the first key in the list being the current one.

Next, hash the received raw payload using the hash algorithm specified in the header value. Finally, create an `RSAPKCS1` deformatter
with the current public key and use it to verify the payload signature.

If verification with the current key fails, attempt verification with the other keys, as the payload may have been signed with an older
key that has since been rotated.

# Making test requests from this page

- Obtain a `SESSION-TOKEN` with the [POST /Authorize/ApiToken](/api-docs/#tag/authorize/POST/Authorize/ApiToken) endpoint.
- Paste `SESSION-TOKEN` as the `Bearer Token` in the `Authentication` box.
- Now all the _"Test Requests"_ can be used.
